taxonomy.note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Anatherum virginicum; Andropogon virginicus is a homotypic synonym and should remain a primary search alias because nearly all Texas field material still uses it.

evidence: Bexar — regional environmental documentation for the San Antonio/Bexar project area explicitly discusses broomsedge (Andropogon virginicus) among the altered-pasture grasses.
Broader Texas native status is clear, but this pass did not lock two additional exact counties inside the project's target zone without inference.
target_zone_range.blocking_issue: Fewer than 3 exact target-zone counties locked in this pass.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Do not infer county occurrence from statewide/ecoregional range.

morphology.look_here_first: Look for narrow silky racemes tucked partly inside flattened spathe-like upper sheaths. Mature plants often turn straw to orange-brown and hold the pale silky seedheads into winter. It does not make the dense brushy crown of bushy bluestem or the digitate turkey foot of big bluestem.
diagnostic_traits: narrow racemes partly enclosed by spathe-like sheaths
silky hairs around spikelets give a pale fluffy look
persistent straw/orange-brown winter clumps are common
2–5 branches per seedhead in common field treatments

confusers.separator: Bushy bluestem has much denser, broader brushlike inflorescence clusters.
Big bluestem has open digitate turkey-foot racemes and a much taller prairie-grass architecture.

installation_guardrail: Do not install as a native canonical species until the 3-county threshold is met.
